top_choice_rationale: Halide perovskites are a materials discovery where structure explains function (ABX3 lattice, defect tolerance, tunable band gap), established by diffraction, microscopy and spectroscopy, with efficiency rising from about 4 percent to above 25 percent and reproduced widely. Miyasaka (first perovskite-sensitized cell), Park (first durable solid-state cell) and Snaith (meso-superstructured and planar architecture) are three documented, distinct founding steps that fit the three-name limit. Stability and lead toxicity are real maturity risks, so if P002 cannot reach a majority I would move to P001, whose two parts are mature, well attributed and chemically distinct.
